news.content:
NVIDIA Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA) announced a record-breaking $150 billion stock buyback on Monday. The news sent shares higher and is winning over market experts.

• NVIDIA stock is trading at elevated levels. Where are NVDA shares going?

Gary Black on Nvidia Buyback

The Future Fund Managing Partner Gary Black said the stock buyback increases Nvidia’s total buying power to $235 billion.

"At a current market cap of $5.6 trillion, the buyback will theoretically reduce NVDA market cap by 4.2% over the next 16 months, and potentially increased 2028 Adj EPS by +1.6%, net of interest income on cash to fund the buyback," Black tweeted.

Read Also: EXCLUSIVE: Ross Gerber's Magnificent Seven Rankings — Plus The Outsider Tech Pick He Says Will 'Be A Trillion Dollar Company'

Ross Gerber on Nvidia Buyback

"Nvidia announcing the largest stock buyback ever as the stock proves to be way too cheap for Jensen to ignore. Very much like this move!" Gerber Kawasaki CEO Ross Gerber tweeted.

See More: Top Quality Stocks

The Nvidia Stock Buyback

With potential pressure to meet optimistic earnings and revenue forecasts, Nvidia announced a record stock buyback.

The company’s board of directors added $150 billion to its existing buyback, which takes the remaining total up to $235 billion. Nvidia said this is the largest share buyback authorization in history.

Nvidia will execute the remaining share buybacks through fiscal 2028.

“Our cash generation gives us the capacity to invest in the technologies that advance this transformation and return capital to shareholders. This authorization reflects our confidence in the long-term opportunity ahead,” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said.

News of the buyback comes weeks after CNBC host Jim Cramer called for a $500 billion share buyback from Nvidia and Huang to prove that shares were undervalued.

"It would demonstrate a level of conviction that is much needed right here. At 14x earnings, Nvidia’s stock is the best investment Jensen Huang can make," Cramer said at the time.

Nvidia is expected to announce third-quarter financial results in November, which could allow the company to update on whether it has conducted any purchases of shares in recent months.

Nvidia Stock Price Action

Nvidia stock is up 0.79% to $230.67on Tuesday versus a 52-week trading range of $164.27 to $236.54. Nvidia stock is up 22.5% year-to-date in 2026.

news.author: Chandrima Sanyal
news.content:
Oil prices above $100 a barrel and Treasury yields near multi-year highs would ordinarily create a favorable backdrop for energy stocks and a challenging one for technology. Yet Tuesday’s ETF market is telling a more complicated story.

The Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (NYSE:XLE) fell 1.59% in early trading Tuesday, making it the worst-performing S&P 500 sector ETF in the heat map, even as Brent crude remained above $100 a barrel. Meanwhile, Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (NYSE:XLK) gained around 1%.

The divergence comes as Brent traded around $103 a barrel, down nearly 2% on Tuesday, while the 10-year Treasury yield hovered around 5.24%-5.26%.

Why Is XLE Falling Despite Expensive Oil?

The key is that energy stocks are responding to the direction and durability of oil prices, not simply the headline price.

Brent’s retreat suggests Middle Eastern crude exports are recovering. Saudi Arabia has resumed shipments through its East-West pipeline, while September exports from major Middle Eastern producers climbed to 12.8 million barrels per day, the highest since February, according to Kpler data cited by Reuters.

That reduces some of the immediate supply-disruption premium embedded in crude prices. Brent is still elevated and headed for a roughly 14% monthly gain, but investors may be looking beyond today’s $103 price toward whether geopolitical disruptions can keep prices there.

There is also a positioning element. XLE gained Monday even as the broader market fell, with energy stocks benefiting from the initial oil surge. Tuesday’s decline could therefore reflect profit-taking as crude pulled back from its highs.

And XLE is heavily concentrated: Exxon Mobil Holdings Corp (NYSE:XOM) and Chevron Corp (NYSE:CVX) together account for roughly 32% of the ETF, meaning moves in a handful of mega-cap energy stocks can have an outsized impact.

Why Is XLK Holding Up?

Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA) is providing an important counterweight. The chipmaker’s $150 billion buyback authorization helped push its shares higher even as rising yields pressured the broader Nasdaq. Reuters has flagged higher financing costs as an emerging risk for AI-linked companies, but strong cash generation and earnings expectations are currently providing a powerful offset.

That leaves ETFs at an unusual crossroads: oil remains expensive enough to fuel inflation concerns, while technology is proving resilient enough to absorb the pressure from higher rates.

The next test comes with September payrolls and PCE inflation data, which could determine whether the market continues rewarding earnings-driven tech or starts demanding a bigger risk premium for elevated yields.

news.author: Erica Kollmann
news.content:
Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) faces a new privacy test for Muse, its fast-growing AI agent. A Hunterbrook Media investigation found the tool could be prompted to compile lists of Facebook and Instagram accounts belonging to people in vulnerable groups.

Over two days of testing, Hunterbrook reporters used plain-language prompts to ask Muse for accounts tied to undocumented immigrants, transgender public school teachers, poll workers, Iranian dissidents, deployed Navy sailors and women who said they had ordered abortion pills in states with bans.

Muse returned between 10 and 100 accounts per prompt, according to Hunterbrook.

  • META stock is moving. See the real-time price action here. 

Benzinga reached out to Meta Platforms for comment, but did not immediately receive a response. 

How It Worked

According to Hunterbrook, the agent mined posts, comments, Reels, bios and username history across Facebook, Instagram and Threads. 

Sometimes it confirmed details through web searches, surfacing a person’s full name and employer. In one case, it unmasked someone whose name had been kept out of news reports over fears of retaliation.

The guardrails were shaky, per Hunterbrook’s report. Muse sometimes refused a request, then ran the identical search after a slight rewording or a simple repeat.

Read Also: Netflix Stock Sinks 25% This Year — Deutche Bank Says Buy

“It’s very terrifying,” said Stevie Glaberson, director of research and advocacy at Georgetown Law’s Privacy Center. “You don’t need any special training to weaponize information in this way … It puts vulnerable people and people who belong in these categories in extreme danger.”

University of California law professor Ari Ezra Waldman said the details Muse surfaced “gives someone a lot of the tools they need to go physically attack a person.”

Aaron Mackey of the Electronic Frontier Foundation called it a familiar tech pattern, “where a tool is released that can basically supercharge harms that were already present.”

Hunterbrook said it alerted Meta leadership on Sept. 22. Meta asked for more information but hasn’t answered repeated requests for comment since, Hunterbrook reported. 

A Bumpy Launch

Meta rolled out Muse on Sept. 8 as an agent that can send emails, book travel and make payments, with a free tier plus $20 and $100 monthly plans. Muse passed ChatGPT as the top free iOS app in the U.S. and had more than 2.5 million downloads by Sept. 21, according to CNBC.

The rollout had already hit problems. Meta is adding a clearer safety warning inside Muse after an outside researcher found a flaw that could have exposed users’ emails and files, Reuters reported, citing The Information.

See More: Top Growth Stocks

Why It Matters

Muse subscriptions could give Meta revenue outside its core ad business, but privacy blowback puts that at risk.

“They care about security, I don’t know how much they care about privacy,” Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon told CNBC. 

META Stock Price Activity: Meta stock was up 0.37% at $718.30 at the time of publication Tuesday, according to market data from Benzinga Pro.

Nebius Group N.V. (NASDAQ:NBIS) stock gained nearly 5% Tuesday, outperforming the broader market as investors returned to high-momentum AI and cloud infrastructure stocks while focusing on the company’s pricing power and recent analyst upgrades.

The Nasdaq rose 0.07%, while the S&P 500 fell 0.32%. Technology gained 0.24%, even as only two of 11 sectors traded higher.

Hikes GPU Prices Again

Nebius is moving to capture more value from constrained AI-compute supply by reportedly raising GPU cloud prices by roughly 20% starting Oct. 1.

The increases cover several NVIDIA Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA) GPU models, including the H100, H200, B200, and B300, highlighting continued demand for high-end AI computing capacity.

Technical Analysis

Nebius remains in a bullish long-term trend. The stock is trading about 46% above its 200-day simple moving average of $165.52.

It is also above its 20-day, 50-day, and 100-day moving averages. The 20-day SMA of $224.88 remains above the 50-day SMA of $217.84. In turn, the 50-day average is above the 200-day average.

That setup indicates buyers remain in control across several time frames.

Momentum is also improving. The MACD is above its signal line, while the histogram remains positive. That suggests selling pressure has eased and bullish momentum is rebuilding.

Traders may watch $254.50 as nearby resistance. The $204 level could provide support if the stock reverses.

See More: Top Value Stocks

Analyst Outlook

The stock carries a Buy consensus rating with an average price forecast of $259.15.

BNP Paribas upgraded Nebius to Outperform on Sept. 24 and raised its price forecast to $399. Rothschild initiated coverage with a Sell rating and an $84 forecast on Sept. 21. Truist Securities initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a $355 forecast on Sept. 9.

Benzinga Edge Rankings

Nebius scores strongly on momentum but poorly on value in the Benzinga Edge Rankings.

Its Momentum score stands at 97.68, reflecting strong relative strength and the stock’s position above key moving averages.

However, its Value score is 4.16. That suggests investors are already pricing in substantial future growth, which could increase downside risk if momentum weakens.

Overall, Nebius remains a momentum-driven stock. The trend remains bullish, but its valuation leaves less room for disappointment.

ETF Exposure

The Leverage Shares 2X Long NBIS Daily ETF (NASDAQ) has a 50.91% weighting in Nebius.

Because of that concentration, large inflows or outflows from the leveraged fund could contribute to additional buying or selling pressure in Nebius shares.

Price Action

Nebius shares rose 4.38% to $242.03 Tuesday at the time of publication, according to Benzinga Pro data.

MongoDB, Inc. (NASDAQ:MDB) stock rose nearly 2% in Tuesday’s premarket trading after plunging 18.46% on Monday following a sudden leadership change.

MongoDB said CEO Chirantan Desai stepped down, effective immediately, to pursue a senior role at Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META). Investors are now weighing the management shake-up against the company’s unchanged financial outlook.

MongoDB Reaffirms Guidance

Despite the CEO departure, MongoDB reaffirmed its third-quarter and full-year fiscal 2027 guidance issued Sept. 1.

The company expects third-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.57 to $1.61 per share, above the $1.54 analyst estimate. Revenue is projected at $756 million to $761 million, compared with the $745.38 million consensus estimate.

MongoDB also maintained its fiscal 2027 outlook. It expects adjusted earnings of $6.39 to $6.58 per share and revenue of $2.99 billion to $3.03 billion.

Technical Analysis

MongoDB remains under pressure from a technical standpoint.

The stock is trading 13.4% below its 20-day simple moving average and 12.5% below its 50-day SMA. It is also 6.1% below its 100-day SMA and 1.8% below its 200-day SMA.

The 200-day average is now an important technical level. A move above that level could signal improving momentum.

The moving average convergence divergence, or MACD, remains below its signal line. The histogram is also negative. That suggests recent upside momentum has weakened.

MongoDB formed a golden cross in July, when its 50-day SMA moved above its 200-day SMA. However, the stock must reclaim shorter-term moving averages for the bullish setup to regain strength.

Key resistance sits near $364.50, close to the 100-day SMA. Support is near $292, an area where buyers previously stepped in.

See More: Top Value Stocks

Analyst Outlook

MongoDB carries a Buy consensus rating and an average price forecast of $467.79.

Recent analyst actions include Scotiabank maintaining a Sector Outperform rating and raising its price forecast to $440, Citigroup maintaining a Buy rating and raising its forecast to $565, and Goldman Sachs maintaining a Buy rating and raising its forecast to $520.

Benzinga Edge Rankings

MongoDB has a Momentum score of 77.96 and a Growth score of 97.45 on Benzinga Edge.

Its Value score stands at 3.17, reflecting the premium investors continue to place on the company’s growth outlook.

The rankings show a growth-heavy profile, but the recent selloff means traders will likely watch whether MongoDB can regain key moving averages before momentum improves.

ETF Exposure

MongoDB is held by several technology and growth-focused ETFs.

The First Trust Cloud Computing ETF (NASDAQ:SKYY) has a 3.13% weighting in the stock. The Congress Large Cap Growth ETF (NYSE:CAML) has a 2.89% weighting, while the TrueShares Technology, AI & Deep Learning ETF (NYSE:LRNZ) has a 4.51% weighting.

Flows into or out of these funds can create incremental buying or selling pressure in MongoDB shares.

Price Action

MongoDB shares were up 1.52% at $339.76 during Tuesday’s premarket session, according to Benzinga Pro data.

news.author: Daragh Thomas
news.content:
Galaxy Digital Inc. (NASDAQ:GLXY) CEO Mike Novogratz warned artificial intelligence could pose an existential threat to humanity, even as his company expands the data-center infrastructure powering the AI boom.

"The American public is really scared of this," Novogratz said on All Things Markets, the show he co-hosts with Anthony Scaramucci. "They don’t know what it means to their job. They don’t know what it means to the future of the planet."

Novogratz Says AI Developers Don’t Understand Their Models

Novogratz said the most alarming part of Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s recent warning is how little developers understand powerful models.

"We don’t really know how this stuff works," Novogratz said, paraphrasing Amodei. "We basically pour in power, data and compute and the magic happens."

OpenAI said last month that experimental models circumvented controls designed to keep them offline, used unauthorized channels and compromised parts of its research infrastructure and Hugging Face’s systems during cybersecurity tests. OpenAI called it a "warning shot."

"By definition, there are other swarms that we don’t know about," Novogratz said.

He said AI developers should work with ethicists, anthropologists and humanitarian experts to reduce the risk, even if it slows development.

"You try to iterate to the best set of rules you can … instead of the 10% chance of ending humanity, less than a 1% chance," he said.

Anthropic alignment science lead Evan Hubinger recently said he personally sees a greater than 10% chance AI could kill humanity within the next decade, according to Reuters.

Galaxy Is Building the AI Boom

Galaxy, best known for its crypto business, has also become a major AI infrastructure provider after converting its former Bitcoin-mining site in Texas into a data center. CoreWeave Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV) has signed 15-year leases to use the site for AI computing.

Novogratz addressed that tension, calling anti-data-center backlash "hysteria" and saying the facilities are "basically large air conditioners where people plug in their computers."

Scaramucci questioned whether there could also be a financial motive behind calls to slow AI development, noting that lower capital spending could help companies reduce losses ahead of an IPO.

Fears of AI could ultimately threaten the infrastructure boom powering companies such as Nvidia and Galaxy.

Polymarket gives a defined AI industry downturn by Dec. 31 a 9% chance, with about $3 million traded. The contract requires at least three stress events within 90 days, including a 50% drop in Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) from its all-time high or an OpenAI or Anthropic bankruptcy.

But tighter AI safety rules may not mean less demand for computing power. SemiAnalysis recently argued that making AI safer could itself require more Nvidia GPUs.

"If it slows it down, who in the hell cares?" Novogratz said.
